request: Make a spec's `## Contracts` rows resolve against the landed diff at drift-check time, exactly as AC ids already do, so a spec cannot promise a function or a CLI that never ships. Resolution keys off the Name cell and never reads the Kind column, which is free text with ~150 distinct values across 636 rows and therefore has no schema to switch on. Evidence of the gap: the spec landed as be0a351 pinned `node .claude/skills/workspace/restore-degraded-shards.mjs [--dry-run]` in its Contracts table; that CLI did not exist and its address contradicted the house `workspace/cli.mjs` front-door convention, yet spec-lint returned PASS on all five checks across three separate approvals, and drift_check could not see it because no AC named the CLI. Only /integrate caught it, by hand, at the last phase before commit. Article VI.4's two-sided rule says YAGNI never authorizes deferring spec-committed scope and no AC row carried a `deferred:` tag, so the spec committed to a capability, the workflow did not build it, and every machine gate stayed green. Weight the design toward under-reporting rather than over-reporting: drift_check gates every spec-track TDD phase, and a false positive yields a workflow that has done nothing wrong.
novelty_evidence: Searched docs/archive/**/spec.md and docs/specs/*.md — 102 of 104 specs carry a Contracts section, 636 rows total. No precedent exists for resolving a Contracts row mechanically: no skill reads the table, and spec-lint's five checks (plantuml_syntax, diagram_presence, ac_traceability, design_calls, system_delta) do not touch it. The obvious precedent, drift_check's AC resolution, does NOT transfer: `AC-\d+` is a pinned token format that spec-lint's ac_traceability already enforces, whereas a Contracts row's Name and Kind cells are prose. The Kind column was measured and is free text — ~150 distinct values, with Function/Fn/fn/fn (export)/Hook fn/Helper all naming one concept — so there is no enum to key a resolver off. The resolvable token has to be invented, which is design work rather than parameterisation of an existing pattern.
track_reason: The leanest safe track is tdd-quickfix — one failing case is known (the be0a351 CLI row) and the change is localized to drift_check.mjs. It is insufficient for two reasons. First, the resolution semantics are undefined anywhere on disk: what token a Contracts row resolves against, how a Function row's signature and a CLI row's invocation each reduce to one, and what a legitimately-unresolvable row looks like are all open, and leaving them only in code repeats the failure this ticket exists to fix. Second, drift_check is the oracle gating every spec-track workflow's TDD phase, so a false positive stops work that is correct; a corpus-wide blast radius over 636 existing rows wants a written contract and gate A. User confirmed spec-entry via AskUserQuestion.
